LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 SENTENCES: COMPLEX SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the role of conjunctions in sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify subordinating conjunctions in sentences
2. construct complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions learnt

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 SENTENCES: COMPLEX SENTENCES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 SENTENCES: COMPLEX SENTENCES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify subordinating conjunctions in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to identify subordinating conjunctions in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify subordinating conjunctions in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify subordinating conjunctions in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions learnt

What this means
In this part you learn to construct complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions learnt. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions learnt.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions learnt. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify subordinating conjunctions in sentences)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences to a partner. (skill: construct complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions learnt)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify subordinating conjunctions in sentences.
3. Practise this skill: construct complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions learnt.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the role of conjunctions in sentences?
2. How can one differentiate between a simple and a complex sentence?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Complex Sentences means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify subordinating conjunctions in sentences.
5. Be able to: construct complex sentences using subordinating conjunctions learnt.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
